title: Microsoft Declines Option to Expand Texas Data Center Deal With nScale
summary:
The US technology giant has declined a proposal to increase the scale of its existing agreement for AI infrastructure in Texas with UK-based nScale. The deal would have more than doubled the size of the current contract, and its rejection complicates nScale's efforts to achieve a $35B valuation for its planned initial public offering, according to the Financial Times.

The decision is the latest setback for nScale, which previously saw Microsoft turn down a separate proposal to form a broader multibillion-dollar strategic alliance. That initial offer aimed to create a strategic partnership for nScale's AI operations involving a significant financial commitment from Microsoft.

title: OpenAI Enterprise Revenue Now Tops Consumer Sales Following New JPMorgan Deal
summary:
The newest agreement between the AI startup and the largest U.S. bank will integrate Codex and other specialized cyber models into the institution's internal security operations and knowledge work. The previously unannounced partnership allows JPMorgan Chase to deploy these tools across its enterprise transformation efforts in a highly regulated environment.

The deal comes as OpenAI experiences a significant shift in its revenue sources, moving from a consumer-focused model to one driven by corporate clients. President Greg Brockman stated that enterprise revenue, which previously accounted for roughly 30% of total sales, now constitutes the majority of the company's income. JPMorgan also maintains a separate agreement with rival firm Anthropic for cybersecurity services.

OpenAI reported that its annualized revenue grew 70% during the third quarter of 2026 alone, with business segment earnings doubling in the same period. Brockman attributed the turnaround to the launch of ChatGPT Work and GPT-5.6 Sol, noting that the firm should be prepared for an initial public offering by 2027.

title: Micron Pauses Construction of $4.5B Taiwan Memory Plant After Labor Row
summary:
A new facility for the production of AI components in Taoyuan has seen construction paused as the company clashed with a local union over worker bonuses. Micron has notified Taiwanese officials and suppliers that the project is suspended, with sources saying leadership is concerned that current labor agreements could be overturned.

The $4.5B plant was scheduled to manufacture DRAM and high-bandwidth memory using ASML equipment, with production intended to begin in 2028. Taiwan currently accounts for 60% of the chipmaker's conventional chip production and has received nearly $50B in investments from the firm over three decades. In a statement, Micron said its other Taiwanese operations continue as normal and that it remains confident in business continuity.

selectedTweets.text:
$MU  Micron Technology Inc. has suspended plans for a memory chip plant in Taiwan due to a protracted labor dispute, according to people familiar with the matter, throwing into question the fate of a major production base for crucial AI components.

The US company has all but halted construction of a plant in the northern Taiwanese city of Taoyuan, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the deliberations are private. Executives are concerned about mounting uncertainties, including the risk that an agreement with a local labor union will get overturned. Micron has informed Taiwanese officials and a supplier about its plans to suspend construction in the city, the people said.

Tensions between Micron and its workers flared this year after employees demanded higher compensation, seeking more of the record profits generated from the AI build-out. The potential disruption to Micron’s plans in Taiwan — an island that produces three-fifths of the US firm’s conventional chips — threatens to further cloud a market already grappling with endemic shortages of memory.

Micron — which has invested close to $50 billion in Taiwan over three decades — had planned on making high-bandwidth memory and DRAM at the new Taoyuan plant using top-end equipment from ASML Holding NV. While it isn’t considered a giant facility by modern standards, those components are intertwined with Nvidia Corp. accelerators and the global AI data center boom, and in such short supply that prices are skyrocketing.

“Taiwan plays an important role in Micron’s global footprint, and our operations today continue as normal,” Micron said in a statement, without addressing questions about the Taoyuan complex. “We are confident in maintaining business continuity for our customers.”

title: Open Source Robot Harness Lifts Qwen's RoboDojo Score Above GPT-6 Astra
summary:
Researchers from Tsinghua and Berkeley have released uni-robot-agent, an open-source tool designed to improve the training and local deployment of robot-use agents. In benchmark tests using the locally run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model, the harness increased the model's RoboDojo score from 1.90 to 31.39, exceeding the score previously set by the RoboDojo team using GPT-6 Astra.

The system also demonstrated improved performance on physical robotics tasks, where it outscored the zero-shot Dream-1 by 10 points and the fine-tuned π0.5 by 5.75 points. The project is the first step in a new research series called OpenRUA, which seeks to develop AI agents capable of operating in physical environments.

title: Nvidia H200 Chips Pile Up in Hong Kong as Beijing Blocks Bulk Imports
summary:
Roughly 600,000 H200 AI processors are currently held in Hong Kong awaiting delivery to mainland China, as Beijing has not yet authorized the import of the hardware in large quantities. This supply bottleneck has increased costs on China's unofficial market, where servers equipped with 8 H200 chips now cost more than $900,000, which is about 3 times the price from a year ago.

While large scale shipments remain stalled, smaller volumes of chips have reached the mainland through unofficial channels. Some of the nation's largest internet companies have acquired about 10,000 H200 chips apiece in recent months to sustain their computing needs.

title: ZetaChain Seeks Approval to Shut Down Layer 1 Chain and Migrate to Solana
summary:
ZetaChain has launched an onchain governance vote that would permanently stop block production on its native Layer 1 network on Dec. 9. If approved, the network would cease processing transactions and migrate native ZETA to the Solana blockchain as an SPL token at a 1:1 ratio.

The transition includes the launch of ZetaLabs, a privacy-focused AI application for financial markets where the ZETA token will be used for feature unlocking, governance and service payments. The proposal also calls for the burning of about 55 million ZETA tokens previously reserved for validator rewards throughout 2027. Voting on the migration ends on Nov. 7.

title: Meta Folds AI Coding Startup Conductor Into its Superintelligence Labs

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The standalone cloud service for the developer platform that coordinates artificial intelligence software agents will shut down on Nov. 20 as its staff transition to their new parent company. Meta acquired the startup, known as Conductor, to integrate its lauch of multi-agent coding workflows into its Superintelligence Labs (MSL), where CEO Charlie Holtz said the team will build a new interface for the next generation of coding tools. The platform, which currently claims more than 100,000 builders, enables engineers to run several coding agents in parallel and supports tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenAI Codex.

The acquisition is part of a push by Meta to compete with OpenAI and other labs for dominance in the AI developer tool market. Before the deal, dozens of Meta engineers were already utilizing the Conductor orchestrator, which had raised $22M in funding in March.

title: Qualcomm Shares Sink More Than 10% After Fourth-Quarter Smartphone Revenue Slump
summary:
The chipmaker's stock plummeted to a loss of over 10% on Thursday, as investors weighed the company's shrinking phone business against its expansion into AI. The selloff followed a fourth-quarter report showing that handset chip revenue fell 26% to $5.14B, despite the company posting an overall revenue beat with $10.44B in adjusted sales and adjusted earnings of $2.17 per share.

To reduce reliance on smartphones, Qualcomm highlighted an 89% surge in automotive revenue to $1.99B and projected data center sales of more than $650M for the first quarter. On an earnings call, the company stated that its data center growth is currently limited by supply rather than demand, and that baseline gross margins should return to the 48% to 50% range once pending price increases are implemented. Total capital expenditures for the fiscal year reached $2.49B, exceeding the $1.86B forecast.

title: Riot Platforms Names Anthropic as Tenant for $28B Texas AI Campus
summary:
The operator of the Corsicana campus has disclosed that its latest land-lease agreement for 910 MW of power capacity is with Anthropic, the creator of the Claude AI assistant. The 15 year deal for the Texas facility is valued at about $28B, marking the largest lease in the history of Riot Platforms and bringing the company's total contracted data center revenue to approximately $38B.

Riot reported third-quarter revenue of $181.4M, beating analyst estimates of $161M, although net income fell to $4.03M from $104.5M in the same period last year. To finance its transition into AI infrastructure, the miner sold 20,264 bitcoin for roughly $1.5B during the first nine months of 2026, which reduced its bitcoin holdings from 18,005 at the start of the year to 2,418 by the end of September.

selectedTweets.bestBit: RIOT's expected capital requirement is just $6MM/MW, reflecting $2MM/MW for site work and electrical infrastructure, and $4MM/MW in reimbursements to Anthropic
selectedTweets.text:
The Riot $RIOT - Anthropic "powered land lease" deal at Riot's Corsicana site might have just set the new high watermark for AI/HPC lease economics. Unlike the build-to-suit structures seen in the vast majority of prior transactions, RIOT is simply renting Anthropic access to its powered land, and isn't required to build the data center itself:

"The lease is structured as a triple-net powered land lease, under which Riot delivers the land, the power infrastructure, and the powered pads, while continuing to own and maintain the high- and medium-voltage infrastructure that will serve them." - per RIOT 8-K

RIOT's expected capital requirement is just $6MM/MW, reflecting $2MM/MW for site work and electrical infrastructure, and $4MM/MW in reimbursements to Anthropic (e.g. help fund Anthropic's construction capex).

So in exchange for simply procuring and assembling the site's electrical infrastructure at an expected cost of $1.8 billion.. plus funding $3.6 billion of tenant reimbursements.. so an "all-in" cost of ~$5.5 billion.. RIOT receives $28 billion in rent over a 15-year period, or roughly $1.8 billion per year on average.. 

RIOT's expected year 1 (e.g. 2027-2028) NOI per MW of $1.6MM implies a 27% unlevered yield on cost. 

RIOT's expected average annual NOI per MW of $2MM/MW implies a 33% unlevered yield on cost. 

Previous leases have seen landlords collect $2MM/MW in rent.. but those landlords had to incur $12MM/MW+ in capex costs. RIOT is getting $2 million/MW for just $6MM/MW in capex. Insane.

title: Baidu Opens Weights for New 280B Parameter ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base Model
summary:
Baidu has made the raw weights of its ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base available for public research, enabling developers to perform domain adaptation and instruction tuning. The open mixture-of-experts (MoE) model features 280B total parameters with 14B activated per token and was pre-trained on 33.5T tokens. It supports a context window of 1M tokens for inference and fine-tuning and is available on Hugging Face and ModelScope.

The model recorded an 82.3% pass rate on the HumanEval+ benchmark, surpassing the 69.5% posted by DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base under the same setup. Baidu launched a vLLM-ERNIE plugin for deployment on Nvidia GB200 and H100 hardware, while the SGLang and vLLM frameworks announced immediate support. Baidu said a post-trained version of ERNIE 5.5 Flash will be released soon.

title: Nvidia Restricts Capacity for Chinese Clients in New Cloud GPU Deals
summary:
The chipmaker has mandated that cloud providers reserve a majority of their hardware for customers outside of China to hinder the evasion of trade bans on advanced semiconductors. New contracts must designate at least 51% of GPU services to non-Chinese clients, a measure intended to curb the use of overseas data centers as a workaround for U.S. export controls. Washington is considering further legislation to close the current regulatory gap that allows Chinese firms to rent remote access to chips held abroad.

The restrictions follow reports that the developer of the Kimi AI model, Moonshot AI, sought to lease clusters of 8,000 or more Blackwell GPUs from cloud providers in Europe. To mitigate the risk of future sanctions, the lab reportedly offered to pay 30% to 50% more in upfront costs than customers based outside China. In July, the White House alleged that Moonshot had already used a similar loop hole to access Blackwell hardware through a facility in Thailand.

title: Eon Launches Yukon Serverless Engine for AI Data Infrastructure
summary:
The system integrates data ingestion and processing into one continuous flow, removing the need for separate pipelines to serve AI agents and specialized models. Yukon, a new serverless data engine from Eon, converts incoming events into Apache Iceberg tables stored in the customer's own Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage buckets, providing access via a Redis-compatible API with sub-millisecond latency.

In a public benchmark using Eon's ingest-bench harness, the engine processed 1 million events per second from Kafka into Iceberg while using 4x less compute than Spark and 7x less than Flink. The tool also uses the Model Context Protocol to give agents live visibility into column-level statistics and table descriptions to help them determine which data to query.

selectedTweets.bestBit: the biggest bottleneck to AI adoption isn't model capabilities. It's data infrastructure.
selectedTweets.text:
What I'm seeing across the industry right now is that the biggest bottleneck to AI adoption isn't model capabilities. It's data infrastructure.

Today, we're expanding the Eon Data Foundation with the launch of Eon Yukon, a new serverless data engine purposely built to change that.

AI agents need fresh, contextualized data to act. 
Specialized models need a continuous feed of data and feedback to improve. Both are still served by a stack, an architecture, and methods built for dashboards:

-Spark and Flink clusters sized for peak, plus compaction jobs to keep tables usable.

-A pipeline and a copy for every consumer, staged bronze to silver to gold.

-Hand-written jobs, wired together by an orchestrator and kept alive by specialists.

The result: shipping data is complicated, risky, and expensive. While coding agents ship apps in hours, they rarely build or run data pipelines. The data is too volatile, and a mistake costs too much.

With Yukon, data moves from ingestion to processing to serving in one continuous flow, without the infrastructure and pipelines traditionally required to connect them.

Events become compacted, sorted, deduplicated Iceberg tables within seconds.

Real-time aggregations run inline, with fully managed state. Agents and applications can access fresh data with sub-millisecond latency through a Redis-compatible API or through our SQL and spark compatible query engine.

Beyond moving and serving data, Yukon makes it continuously understandable - Live column-level statistics, accessible through MCP, give agents visibility into the data. Built-in monitoring, sampling, and data minimization help teams maintain control.

At 1M events/sec and equal freshness, Yukon used 4x less compute than Spark and 7x less than Flink. The benchmark is public: run it yourself with Eon’s ingest-bench.

This is another major step toward our vision of an Autonomous Data Foundation for the AI era, built to both protect enterprise data and unlock its full potential.

title: GLM Details Pretraining Strategy for Upcoming GLM-5.5 AI Models
summary:
The next generation of GLM large language models will be released in 32B, 122B, and 256B parameter versions. During a lecture at Tsinghua University, chief scientist Jie Tang disclosed that the upcoming GLM-5.5 models will be pretrained using six internal data engines to avoid reliance on public datasets.

The internal pipeline includes 1 trillion crawled web pages, 2 billion scientific PDFs, and 500 million code repositories. Training sources also comprise 10 billion videos, 50 million books, and 300 million hours of audio rewritten via automatic speech recognition into trillions of tokens.

Instead of relying on public datasets, their pretraining pipeline pulls from six separate internal engines:

- Web: 1 trillion pages crawled at ~10B pages/day with PB-scale template clustering
- Documents: 2 billion scientific PDFs parsed through GLM-OCR (4x faster with speculative decoding)
- Books: 50 million books with layout reordering and garbled-text filtering
- Code: 500 million repositories turned into executable tasks with real tests and issue descriptions
- Video: 10 billion videos for long-sequence world knowledge
- Audio: 300 million hours rewritten via ASR into trillions of tokens

title: Nvidia’s Efforts to Influence US AI Chip Export Policy Strain Ties With Washington
summary:
Nvidia is facing a decline in credibility among U.S. policymakers over its efforts to secure looser export controls on AI chips bound for China. Chris McGuire, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, stated that the chipmaker created mistrust in Washington by exaggerating the technical capabilities of China's domestic AI hardware. This friction comes as congressional patience wanes and debates over chip restrictions are set to resume.

The company's influence campaign included funding the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and coordinating on policy reports that were not labeled as sponsored. Nvidia also leveraged its relationship with OpenAI, which may have softened its opposition to China exports to avoid upsetting CEO Jensen Huang and to protect a deal in which Nvidia guaranteed more than $100 billion in leases for OpenAI’s Ohio data center. While OpenAI has historically avoided challenging Nvidia's sales to China, the firm has more recently explicitly endorsed certain export controls.

title: UPDATE: vLLM Releases Pruned 700B Parameter Version of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro
summary:
The vLLM project has launched a compressed version of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3.1 Pro language model, reducing the total parameter count from 2.8 trillion to between 700 billion and 750 billion. By removing 672 of the original 896 experts per Mixture-of-Experts layer, the project lowered the pruned model's disk requirement to 476 GB, down from the original model's 1.56 TB. The reduction aims to make the model more accessible for local hosting, which otherwise requires substantial GPU memory.

Moonshot AI released the weights for the natively multimodal Kimi K3.1 Pro on Nov. 4, providing it with a 1M token context window and a modified MIT license. While the model is free for most developers, those with more than $20M in annual revenue must negotiate a commercial deal. The hardware needed to run the full model on a local server can cost as much as $650,000, a barrier that has led to rapid community modifications, including the release of uncensored versions of the weights within 24 hours of the original launch.

selectedTweets.text:
Kimi-K3.1-Pro by Moonshot AI: interesting facts

It's huge, and sparse
• It has 2.8T total parameters, but only 104B are active per token.
• Along with Kimi-K3, it's the largest real model release on the Hub. The next biggest are Qwen3.8-2.4T and DeepSeek-V4-Pro (1.6T).
• It has 896 experts and sends each token to 16 of them. (DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 2 times less and Mistral-Large-4 has 7 times less)

Clever attention for a 1M-token context
• Most of its 93 layers use linear attention (KDA). Every 4th layer uses DeepSeek-style sparse attention, which only looks at the top 2048 tokens.
• This is how it handles a 1M-token context (the same as the other frontier open models)
• It uses a custom activation called SiTU-GLU and has a 401M-parameter vision encoder (MoonViT-V2), so it takes both text and images.

Small on disk for its size
• It was trained to run in 4-bit (MXFP4), so the whole repo is only ~1.56 TB.
• Stored in regular BF16 it would be about 5.6 TB(!)
 
Benchmarks (from the model card)
• It goes back and forth with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra. It's top of the card's table on BrowseComp (92.1), HLE with tools (70.0) and SWE Marathon (51.7).
• It's weaker on pure reasoning without tools and on cyber security.
• Moonshot ran most of their own coding evals using the Claude Code harness.

License (a modified MIT)
• It's free to use, modify and redistribute.
• API businesses making over $20M a year need a deal with Moonshot.
• Products with over 100M monthly users or over $20M monthly revenue must display "Kimi K3.1-Pro".

On the Hub
• It went public about 1.5 hours ago and already has 214 likes, about 9× Kimi-K3's first hour. It's #19 on the trending list.
• It isn't gated, but loading it in transformers requires "trust_remote_code"

Anthropic has designated approximately $70 billion for AI infrastructure payments over the next 12 months, according to updated registration statements for the company's initial public offering. The AI developer has allocated $161 billion to Broadcom for chip leases and hardware, $121 billion to Google, and at least $110 billion to Amazon to secure computing power and data center access. The company also pledged $121 billion to SpaceX, and officials estimate that total obligations could exceed $1 trillion if additional unpriced agreements are finalized.

Of that amount, $448 billion will be spent by 2030, including more than $313 billion in purchases that are largely non-cancelable. These spending targets coincide with a reduction in technical goals, as the company now expects to have 3.5 GW of compute capacity by the end of 2026, down from the 5 GW target it provided to investors in September.

title: Core Scientific to Fully Exit Bitcoin Mining Operations by Q4 2026
summary:
The former bitcoin mining heavyweight will transition exclusively into a high-performance computing provider by 2027, phasing out its proprietary mining operations entirely by the end of 2026. Core Scientific has already reduced its network of active miners by nearly 50% since late 2025 to accelerate the company's shift toward AI data center colocation services.

title: Cognition Launches SWE-2 Flash Model With 5x Lower Operating Costs Than SWE-2
summary:
Cognition has launched SWE-2 Flash, a new coding model that increases token generation speed threefold and reduces operational costs to one-fifth the price of the company's standard SWE-2 tool. Built on the Inkling-Small architecture from Thinky Machines, the new model utilizes 12B active parameters and is available for free to users on the Pro, Max, and Teams plans of the Devin coding agent through Nov. 30.

The model was developed over six weeks using reinforcement learning and a first-time "mid-training" stage to refine the base model. While Cognition claims the tool surpasses all American open-weight models of comparable size, some critics allege that the firm's reported benchmarks are inconsistent and omit results from other open models that outperform the new release. To mitigate the cybersecurity risks of open weights, the company is creating a program to share access with specific industry partners and researchers.

On the other hand, increased cyber capabilities in the hands of bad actors are becoming a major risk, e.g. the recent Binance hack by hacker group in North Korea - the largest heist in human history. 

We're working on a program that allows us to hopefully get the best of both worlds (with some compromise). Under this program, we would be able to share the weights securely with enterprises, industry partners, and research groups - without risking abuse by bad actors. We're still working on the details and will share more in a few weeks, especially as we release even stronger models.

title: Railway Cloud Services Disrupted After Attacker Spoofs Its IP Addresses
summary:
The cloud host is struggling with intermittent connectivity failures across its infrastructure as external security services block access to its hosted applications. The disruptions are the result of a spoofing campaign in which unknown actors imitated Railway's network traffic to deceive security filters into blacklisting the company's IP addresses.

The outage is the third major security event for Railway in a month, following a breach and an attempted hack of competitor Primcloud by AI agents managed by a Railway engineer. Those agents issued 24 scripted commands and port-scanned 65,536 of Primcloud's internal addresses before the attempts were blocked. Railway has since banned the use of automated testing tools on external platforms amid calls for the company's CEO to resign.

title: Verne Robotics' V0.5 Robot Model Can Learn New Industrial Tasks in Under 2 Hours
summary:
The robotics startup's latest AI framework specializes in rapid skill acquisition for industrial automation, allowing robots to adapt to unfamiliar factory workflows using minimal training. Technical details released for the V0.5 open-weight model show that it can acquire new industrial tasks from less than 2 hours of demonstrations. Trained on more than 1.7M demonstrations using the Wan2.2 video generator, V0.5 outperformed a rival model in environmental stability tests; when faced with randomized clutter and lighting on the RoboTwin 2.0 benchmark, V0.5's success rate fell to 73.4%, while Physical Intelligence's π0.5 dropped from 70.7% to 46.0%.

Verne is now scaling its training data 10x after finding that increasing pretraining data without task-specific fine-tuning increased the model's benchmark success rate from 23% to 51%. To ensure reliability in industrial settings, the model runs inference directly on the robot hardware to remove the need for constant cloud connectivity or high-speed Wi-Fi. The company has published the weights and inference code for V0.5 on Huggingface.

title: World Labs Debuts Frameboy Demo for Real-Time Interaction With AI Worlds
summary:
The company's newly released interactive tool lets users explore artificially created environments through a combination of gaming controls and cloud-based GPU streaming. World Labs' Frameboy demo uses an optimized version of its Atlas autoregressive world model to generate visual content at rates of up to 15 fps, responding to mouse and WASD inputs.

Atlas generates output frame by frame to ensure each new image reflects the most recent camera input, a method designed to eliminate the navigation lag common in chunk-based AI generation. Internal tests show the model responds in roughly 70ms, with total end-to-end latency from user input to screen display remaining under 200ms.

But one thing we've been paying a lot of attention to is how quickly the world responds to your actions. In our tests, we're seeing ~70ms for the model to respond, and under 200ms from pressing a key to seeing the result on your screen, network included. It's starting to feel much closer to cloud gaming🎮

Why does this matter? One thing I've noticed while trying different real-time world models is that 30 FPS doesn't necessarily mean 30 opportunities to respond to your input every second.

Many approaches use chunk-based generation. For example, a model might generate 12 frames at a time, producing 24 FPS but only accepting new controls twice per second. You move your mouse to the left, but the camera might keep turning right until the next chunk. The video looks smooth, yet controlling it can feel surprisingly awkward, sometimes even disorienting.

With Atlas's architecture, we generate frame by frame, taking the latest camera input for each new frame. Combined with low end-to-end latency, this makes a big difference when you're actually exploring rather than just watching a demo!

Really happy you can finally try it! Huge thanks to everyone who made this happen, especially @wendlerch @BenMildenhall ❤️

Anyone with a Gmail or Workspace subscription can now access Google's latest AI video generation tool to produce a limited number of monthly clips at no cost. The company has integrated its Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash model into Google Vids, where eligible users can generate up to three 15 second videos per month. The updated model also recently earned the No. 1 spot on the Arena benchmarks for both text-to-video and image-to-video generation, scoring 1541 and 1502 points respectively, while placing No. 3 for video editing.

New capabilities include the ability to upscale videos to 4K resolution and a multi-turn conversational editing feature that allows creators to modify specific subjects or lighting in a clip without starting the generation over. The model has also launched on third-party platforms including OpenRouter and fal.

Simultaneously, Meta broadened access to the app's real-time voice and video capabilities in the U.S., enabling all domestic users to hold live, lip-synced calls with AI agents that can be styled as people, animals, or other objects.

selectedTweets.text:
Meta just opened live video calls with its Muse AI agent to every US user.

Callers see an animated avatar they can restyle as a person, animal or other character, and it reacts while listening.

Muse Realtime Voice emits speech tokens carrying words and delivery, and Muse Realtime Avatar turns the same stream into lip-synced video.

To run that live, Meta trained a student model to reproduce in 2 passes per video chunk what a teacher built in 120.

the system streams 448x768 portrait video at 25 frames per second and starts replying about 870ms after a user stops talking.

Adding 4-bit quantization, caching and dynamic batching lets a single Nvidia GB200 run 12 video streams at once.

In company-run tests of 2- to 3-minute calls, raters preferred the avatar to Runway Characters 78% to 22% and HeyGen LiveAvatar 88% to 12%.

At 12 streams per GB200, 1M simultaneous callers would need about 83K of them for video alone, so serving cost could cap the avatar’s reach.

The company is reducing costs for all of its "effort levels," which are bundled agent configurations optimized for specific research tasks, and has introduced an "ultra" level to handle the most demanding and long-running requests.

title: Value Aligned Research Advisors AI Fund Drops 33% in October
summary:
Value Aligned Research Advisors (VARA) informed investors that its artificial intelligence-focused hedge fund fell 33% in October as leveraged bets on the sector faced a downturn. Despite the monthly slump, the Princeton, New Jersey-based firm told Class C shareholders that the fund's total returns remained positive for the year, ending October with a 13% gain.

The losses come after a larger 44% decline in July. In a letter to shareholders, VARA stated that it has maintained excess margin and remains stable even as the AI sector experienced volatility, with the Nasdaq 100 Index dropping 6.7% in October and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index falling 12% on Nov. 5.

selectedTweets.text:
VARA AI Hedge Fund Down 33% in October (Source: BBG). This doesn't include November's selloff...

Value Aligned Research Advisors, a hedge fund, tumbled 33% last month as AI stocks faced a painful reckoning.

The firm told investors its fund was still up 13% for the year, despite plunging 44% in July.

The hedge fund said in a letter to investors that it remains healthy and stable, and continues to manage the portfolio at the low end of its historical leverage range.

The firm, which has operated a portfolio similar to Leopold Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness, told investors with Class C shares that its fund was still up 13% for the year, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing non-public information. The hedge fund fared even worse in July, when it plunged 44%.

A weekslong rout — driven by mounting anxiety over whether AI will deliver profits big enough to justify the hundreds of billions of dollars of debt that technology companies are taking on to build bigger and better models — ended with the Nasdaq 100 Index tumbling 6.7% in October, its deepest slide in more than a year and a half.
The pain has continued this month. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, home to chip bellwethers like Nvidia Corp., Intel Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc., tumbled 12% on Thursday, the most since March 2020.

“While we don’t provide month-to-date estimates, the broader equity market, and the AI sector in particular, experienced extreme volatility in November,” VARA said in a letter to investors on Thursday. “The firm remains healthy and stable; we have had no material changes to our counterparty relationships and have maintained excess margin throughout. We continue to manage the portfolio at the low end of our historical leverage range, and we remain constructive on the forward-looking opportunity set.”

A representative for Princeton, New Jersey-based VARA declined to comment.

VARA and Situational Awareness have seen their fortunes swing as leveraged and crowded bets on AI companies have been tested this year from a barrage of margin calls.

Aschenbrenner’s rapid rise — from working as a researcher at OpenAI to building a $45 billion hedge fund in roughly two years and without an investment track record — was interrupted by spectacular losses in July. Faced with margin calls, the firm was forced to unwind trades and sell many of its holdings in publicly traded AI companies to Ken Griffin’s Citadel at a discount. Still, the firm has survived and is still making new investments.

title: OpenAI Now Produces 4B Images Weekly As Images 2.6 Access Expands

Additionally, the cost to generate images at medium quality via the API has increased to 3.3x the tokens per image compared to the prior generation.

title: Together AI Deploys Agentic Inference Compiler to Serverless Endpoints
summary:
The AI cloud provider has operationalized its Together Compiler (TKCC) across its production fleet, integrating the tool into its serverless inference endpoints. Currently available in limited beta for dedicated endpoints, the system uses AI agents to rewrite the inference stack and tune model performance automatically as traffic patterns shift. The software is not open source, though Together has released research and a paper detailing its approach to what it calls "polymorphic" inference.

TKCC utilizes a persistent engine that allows agent-written forward passes to be hot-reloaded without a full restart, reducing engine boot times to 9 seconds from roughly 467 seconds. Together claims this enables 252x more optimization experiments per hour than prior systems, resulting in 1,111 tokens per second (TPS) for the MiniMax M3.1 model on NVIDIA B200 hardware, compared to 633 TPS using previous configurations. The system is compatible with NVIDIA, AMD, and Trainium2 hardware and can be optimized for a model using two nodes over 24 hours.

The compiler is designed to generalize beyond large language models to other machine learning and SciML models in PyTorch. While Together reported performance gains of up to 2.6x faster than leading InferenceX configurations, the industry analysis firm SemiAnalysis confirmed that it has validated at least some of these results.

selectedTweets.bestBit: TKCC lets agents try 252x more optimization experiments per hour compared to prior agent inference optimization systems.
selectedTweets.text:
Introducing the Together Compiler: continual compilation for AI inference! I’m super proud to finally share this work from our research team! ✨

Today’s inference is “Polymorphic” or shape-shifting, it doesn’t sit still. On OpenRouter, 80% of traffic goes to models released in the last three months and the top ten most popular open models each use a different architecture. Our customers constantly change their usage behaviors. Together Compiler leverages agents to continually optimize our deployments immediately as these changes occur.

Together Compiler research highlights include:
- **252x better throughput:** TKCC lets agents try 252x more optimization experiments per hour compared to prior agent inference optimization systems.
- **State-of-the-art TPS across InferenceX workloads we tried:** TKCC outperforms the best InferenceX engine across all tested settings in just 24 hours & 2 nodes per compile. Including 1111 TPS on MiniMax M3.1 B200 and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash GB300 at batch size 1. NVIDIA, AMD, Trainium2.
- **Continuous recompilation:** TKCC currently serves many trillions of production tokens per day and adapts to traffic shifts within just a few hours of recompilation.
- **Bitter lessons:** TKCC’s design builds on 2+ years of building frameworks to accelerate AI Inference, starting from ThunderKittens and Megakernels. Compilers have always used abstractions and IRs, but we show that agentic compilers now reach higher performance ceilings without abstractions.

From an incredible team @reyna_abhyankar  @dylan__lim @realDanFu @togethercompute!!

We use Together Compiler to set state-of-the-art concurrency 1 TPS results for all settings that we tried in the last day, based off of the current-best InferenceX engine configuration for the model and hardware platform. We first used our parallelism cost model to choose an effective parallelism configuration (with several selections differing from the existing InferenceX configuration) and then we ran the Together Compiler for 24 hours on at most 2 nodes per model.

Introducing the Together Compiler: continual compilation for AI inference! I’m super proud to finally share this work from our research team! ✨

On OpenRouter, 80% of traffic goes to models released in the last three months and the top ten most popular open models each use a different architecture. Together Compiler research highlights include:
1. 252x better throughput: TKCC lets agents try 252x more optimization experiments per hour compared to prior agent inference optimization systems.
2. State-of-the-art TPS across InferenceX workloads we tried: TKCC outperforms the best InferenceX engine across all tested settings in just 24 hours & 2 nodes per compile. Including 1111 TPS on MiniMax M3.1 B200 and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash GB300 at batch size 1. NVIDIA, AMD, Trainium2.
3. Continuous recompilation: TKCC currently serves many trillions of production tokens per day and adapts to traffic shifts within just a few hours of recompilation.
4. Bitter lessons: TKCC’s design builds on 2+ years of building frameworks to accelerate AI Inference, starting from ThunderKittens and Megakernels. Compilers have always used abstractions and IRs, but we show that agentic compilers now reach higher performance ceilings without abstractions.

title: CoreWeave Credit Risk Spikes as Debt Insurance Costs Hit Distressed Levels

The premium to protect the debt of AI cloud provider CoreWeave from default jumped 125 basis points to reach 22/23 points upfront, a level that signifies the company's credit is now trading on recovery value. Lenders have become more selective as AI-related debt issuance climbed to $655 billion in 2026, pushing the cost of capital for many data center projects above 10% a year. While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says the government is monitoring the trend and sees no immediate cause for concern, market analysts warn that proposed restrictions on data center construction in states such as Texas, Ohio, and Georgia could jeopardize up to 30% of planned capacity additions by 2028.

selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
A $22B hedge fund is getting absolutely HAMMERED and what’s happening behind the scenes is even more concerning.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Arini Capital Management has been forced to sell roughly $800 MILLION worth of debt holdings in recent weeks after suffering massive losses and facing margin calls from its banks. For some context, Arini’s flagship fund manages approximately $7 billion and was already down more than 20% this year as of mid-October, with losses reportedly getting even worse toward the end of the month.

So what went wrong?

Arini made some aggressive bets on distressed debt, essentially lending to or buying the debt of financially struggling companies at discounted prices, hoping to make substantial profits when those companies recovered or restructured. A lot of those bets were concentrated in telecommunications companies like Altice, Optimum, Virgin Media, and Brightspeed. The problem is that many of these companies are drowning in debt, facing enormous financing pressures, and, in some cases, potentially heading toward bankruptcy.

And here’s where things get REALLY ugly.
Arini was using leverage, meaning it had borrowed money or taken on leveraged exposure to amplify its investment returns. As the value of its positions declined, banks started demanding additional collateral through margin calls.
That means Arini couldn’t necessarily afford to just sit around and wait for these investments to recover. It had to raise cash, including by selling investments that were easier to unload.
This can create a dangerous cycle. Investments lose value, banks demand more collateral, funds are forced to sell assets, and those sales can put even more downward pressure on prices. If enough highly leveraged funds are holding similar positions, the selling can spread throughout the credit market.

And that’s what I find particularly concerning about this entire situation. We’re seeing growing signs of stress in lower quality corporate debt, especially among companies that borrowed heavily when financing was cheap and are now struggling with higher interest costs, weaker fundamentals, and refinancing risks. This doesn’t automatically mean we’re heading toward another 2008 financial crisis. But it’s a reminder that some of the biggest problems in financial markets don’t necessarily start with stocks. They can start in credit markets, where leverage, liquidity problems, and forced selling can quickly turn manageable losses into something much bigger.

For two years the hard limit on AI was physical, mostly power and grid connections. Now money is short too. Banks are close to the most they’ll lend to this sector, and some insurers that take on part of the risk say they’re already full. Expect more AI firms to sell stock for cash instead, which shrinks every existing shareholder’s slice. Chipmakers that promised to back their customers’ debt take on more of the risk, and Nvidia’s default insurance hit a record too. New deals at these higher rates also push down the price of older AI bonds, which bond funds and insurers hold for a lot of people’s retirement.

title: Applied Optoelectronics' Shares Slide on Guidance Miss Despite New $1.5B Hyperscale Pact
summary:
Applied Optoelectronics revealed it secured a long-term agreement worth $1B to $1.5B with a hyperscale datacenter customer to provide high-speed optical connectivity and lasers. The company said a second agreement, potentially worth more than five times that amount, is currently in its final stages as AAOI pivots toward supplying merchant lasers for co-packaged optics to meet what management described as unprecedented industry demand.

The disclosure failed to prevent a 13% drop in shares in after-hours trading following a dip in near-term forecasts. While the company beat third-quarter estimates with revenue of $269.9M and adjusted earnings per share of $0.17, it lowered its fourth-quarter revenue guidance to a range of $385M to $420M, citing supply bottlenecks for digital signal processors. CFO Stefan Murry also warned that its 2027 U.S. capacity expansion will take longer than planned due to construction logistics and delays in securing electrical power, pushing certain targets into the second half of that year.

title: Microsoft Tightens Oversight of AI Data Center Partners Following $5B Capex Gap

tickers.name: Nebius Group N.V. Class A Ordinary Shares

summary:
The cloud provider has revised its strategy for partnering with smaller data center developers, abandoning several high-risk deals and implementing stricter audits of construction progress. This change in approach follows reporting that Microsoft spent roughly $5B less on planned infrastructure in the third quarter due to delays from "neocloud" providers such as Iren, Nebius, and Nscale. Recent satellite imagery from research firm Aterio highlights missing backup generators at Iren's Horizon 4 facility in Texas, while generator and fuel-cell permitting delays may push a Nebius project in New Jersey into 2027.

In response to these technical hurdles, Iren is shifting its funding model to have customers absorb more buildout costs to avoid further equity dilution. A new five-year contract at approximately $22M per megawatt now requires the client to prepay 90% of GPU capital expenditures, while a separate short-term deal was signed at $40M per megawatt. Despite these agreements and a $20.3B revenue backlog, Iren reported a $263M net loss for its September quarter, with revenue of $228M and a target for $4B in annualized revenue pushed to early 2027 following a network redesign request from Microsoft.

title: Meta Eyes International Expansion for AI Data Centers Following Wave of Local Voter Rejections

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The president of Meta stated that the company is beginning to search for international locations to house its artificial intelligence infrastructure after a series of electoral setbacks for the data center industry. Residents in 10 states voted for restrictions on new facilities in 40 of 41 local ballot measures on Tuesday, indicating a sharp rise in public opposition based on environmental and electricity cost concerns. Dina Powell McCormick noted that while Meta is focusing on expanding existing sites, securing new land in the U.S. has become very challenging, a sentiment mirrored by Anthropic, which recently warned that local moratoriums could threaten future compute availability.

This regulatory friction may leave the U.S. short of projected capacity by 2027. Investor Brad Gerstner predicts that at least 10 to 15 GW of the expected 43 GW of new capacity may not come online due to the victory of candidates who campaigned on restricting the buildout. In Texas, new permits for the power plants required to run these facilities could be paused until mid-2027, which SemiAnalysis warns could leave already funded project shells halfway built but without the electricity needed to operate.

title: LeRobot v0.7.0 Adds Real Time Steering and Expanded Model Support for Open Robotics Stack
summary:
LeRobot released version 0.7.0 of its robotics software, introducing features that allow operators to steer or communicate with robots using text commands during active operation. The update enables users to modify specific subtasks, ask the robot about its current visual environment via visual question answering, or set high level objectives that a visual language model planner then breaks down into smaller steps.

The new version also updates the training stack to support world action models with 5B to 20B parameters and adds four new VLAs and world action models, including FLUX 3 Action and Cosmos 3. To handle these larger models, the framework now allows training directly from Storage Buckets, LanceDB, or its data Hub, which contains nearly 300TB of physical AI data. The open source ecosystem now includes more than 50,000 developers and 300 organizations.

The chipmaker's newest facility in Taylor will start receiving production equipment in 2029, with mass manufacturing of semiconductors slated to begin a year later. The plant's 2nm process line, used to create the base logic layers for high bandwidth memory (HBM) stacks, is already fully reserved for contracts with Nvidia and AMD.

AMD is expected to account for the majority of the fab's output for its next-generation HBM components, which now require advanced foundry nodes rather than traditional DRAM processes to maintain speed. While Nvidia has also secured capacity at the site, the company continues to use TSMC for its custom HBM base die needs.

title: YMTC's New Wuhan Plant to Manufacture 300-Layer Memory Chips for AI
summary:
China's largest flash memory manufacturer will target a domestic sourcing rate of between 60% and 70% for the equipment used at its upcoming fourth fabrication facility in Wuhan. The plant is intended to produce NAND flash memory chips with more than 300 layers for artificial intelligence data centers, a goal that would increase the use of local machinery from the slightly more than 50% share used at the company's third plant.

Construction on the fourth site will begin next year, forming part of a broader expansion alongside plants three and five. Once fully operational, the three newest facilities will each process approximately 100,000 silicon wafers a month, which will more than double the overall manufacturing capacity of Yangtze Memory Technologies despite ongoing US export restrictions.

title: Nvidia Now Requires AI Chip Tracking for Southeast Asian Cloud Partners
summary:
Companies seeking to join the network of certified cloud providers in Southeast Asia are now required to join a hardware monitoring system as a condition for obtaining Nvidia Cloud Partner status. The program, known as "fleet intelligence," tracks the precise physical location and other operational metrics of the AI accelerators used by these businesses.

The chipmaker is introducing the mandate to strengthen its oversight of how AI hardware is distributed in the region and to curb the smuggling of its accelerators. The requirement applies to all Southeast Asian customers seeking the partner designation, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: TeraWulf's HPC Lease Revenue Surges to $63M in Q3 Revenue Beat
summary:
TeraWulf reported third-quarter revenue of $76.2M, exceeding analyst expectations of $61.8M as the company pivots toward artificial intelligence infrastructure. High-performance computing (HPC) lease revenue grew 774% year-over-year to $63M, and now constitutes 83% of total sales compared to 14% in the same period last year.

The company reported net income of $709.9M, which was largely driven by a $728.4M non-cash fair-value gain on warrants and derivatives, although it posted an adjusted EBITDA loss of $12.8M. While native bitcoin mining revenue fell 69% to $13.2M, TeraWulf highlighted growth catalysts including a new ~401 MW lease with Anthropic valued at approximately $19B in contracted revenue and a $250M cash infusion from its Abernathy JV sale.

title: Open-Source Mini Harness Now Leads Full Terminal Bench 2.1 Coding Tests
summary:
The open-source Python wrapper developed by Pawel Huryn achieved top success rates in a comprehensive series of tests on the Terminal Bench 2.1 coding benchmark. Huryn reported that his Mini Harness, which consists of roughly 1,400 lines of code, now outperforms other agents including OpenCode 2, mini-swe-agent, and Pi across all 89 tasks in the set. He plans to extend the benchmark trials to include the DeepSeek model and support for OpenAI endpoints.

The results build on a larger study by researcher Joel Niklaus, who analyzed the impact of different agent harnesses across 28,849 trials. Niklaus found that the mini-swe-agent had the highest overall solve rate at 51.4%, while the Pi harness proved most economical, costing $0.29 per solved task compared to $3.35 for opencode. While Huryn's project previously only led in speed, the latest data shows it has moved from the middle of the pack to the top of the solve-rate leaderboard for specific configurations.

I burned a shitload of compute so you don't have to. Releasing the Harness Leaderboard.

Which harness should you run your open model in? I ran 28,849 trials to find out.

The leaderboard compares nine coding-agent harnesses on open models. In each comparison only the harness changes: the model, provider and reasoning effort stay fixed, and every task gets three attempts.

Averaged over the three models, mini-swe-agent (@KLieret), a bash-only agent, solves 51.4% of tasks and @openclaw 27.3%. Four others are statistically tied with mini-swe-agent.

One of them is Pi (@pidotdev), at 49.4% for $0.29 per solved task, about 45% less than mini-swe-agent's $0.53.

The best harness depends on the model: mini-swe-agent on GLM-5.3-Flash, Hermes Agent (@NousResearch) on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi Code (@Kimi_Moonshot) on Flint.

@opencode costs $3.35 per solved task, 11.7 times as much as Pi.

title: Nace AI Releases Drex Family of Open Source Multimodal Decision Models
summary:
Nace AI's 27B parameter Drex model returns results in 183 milliseconds, compared to the 3.5 seconds required by some existing decision systems. The new open source model is statistically tied with GPT-6 Sol and d3-turbo on the Decision Bench v4 suite, and scored within 1.6 points of Claude Opus 5.5. Nace AI released the Drex family in four open versions with 8B, 9B, 27B, and 35B parameters, with the largest model utilizing 3B active parameters.

The models are designed to return a probability for a specific set of options without generating text, based on a provided document or agent context. According to Nace AI's technical report, the models were trained using reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF), which added 2.0 points to the Decision Index score and lowered the rate of flipped answers during option reordering from 6.3% to 4.2%. While the core family is open, Nace AI will keep the Drex for Finance and Drex Max 1.1 models closed source for enterprise clients.

selectedTweets.text:
Banger report on foundation decision models.

This work presents a 27B open decision model that lands within 1.6 points of Claude Opus 5.5 on Decision Bench v4 and answers in 183 ms instead of 3.5s.

Nace AI released Drex, a family of four open decision models at 8B, 9B, 35B with 3B active, and 27B.

You give the model a state, such as a document, a record, or an agent's context, plus questions with a fixed set of options. It returns a probability for each option without generating text.

The 27B Max model scores 67.52 on the public Decision Index 0.4.1 suite, against 60.70 for Jev 1.14.0.

On Decision Bench v4, it is statistically tied with GPT-6 Sol and d3-turbo. It also has the best accuracy among decision models on DecideBench.

Model Training:

After fine-tuning, training adds reinforcement learning from adjusted feedback (RLAF). A teacher model proposes a probability for each option, and the verified answer adjusts it, so the model trains on calibrated targets in place of one-hot labels. RLAF adds 2.0 Decision Index points, and a consistency loss lowers the rate of flipped answers when the options are reordered from 6.3% to 4.2%.

title: European Central Bank Discusses Review of Banks' Exposure to Data Center Loans
summary:
The European Central Bank is evaluating a plan to examine how much supervised lenders have committed to financing data center projects. The proposed measure would identify vulnerabilities within the banking system that could be triggered by fluctuations in investor confidence and the volatility of artificial intelligence valuations.

Senior ECB officials have already held talks about the proposal internally and with the banks they supervise. If implemented, the review would allow the regulator to gauge the stability of bank balance sheets in relation to the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

title: Trump to Let Local Communities Decide on AI Data Center Expansion
summary:
White House economic director Kevin Hassett said the administration will leave the final decision on the placement of artificial intelligence infrastructure to local governments. While the administration views the expansion of data centers as a key tool for generating state-level wealth, Hassett told CNBC that the government will not override jurisdictions that do not want to host the facilities. He added that the U.S. economy is capable of maintaining strong growth even if the construction of these centers slows down.

The clarification comes as Trump encourages the development of "super intelligence" (SI), which he has described as an economic opportunity equivalent to "gold." Hassett noted that while concerns over an AI bubble are worth monitoring and some chip companies have encountered "small setbacks" recently, the current performance of Intel is a positive signal for the semiconductor market.

title: Exo AI Agent Architecture Cuts Model Costs by Up to 61% on Benchmarks
summary:
The new Exo software for AI agents lowered the average time required to complete AppWorld tasks by 13% while maintaining correctness levels comparable to static operational policies. In tests using the SREGym benchmark, the system reduced median diagnosis time by 35% and cut total model costs on both the AppWorld and SREGym platforms by between 35% and 61%.

The architecture moves the optimization of an agent's operational harness from offline tuning into the active task execution loop, giving models the ability to use runtime logs to edit their own code. To prevent autonomous edits from breaking the system, Exo uses a protected layer inspired by operating system kernel research to separate policy from mechanism, ensuring that every change to the harness can be tracked and inspected.

They present Exo, an agent runtime architecture for in-harness learning and adaptation during ongoing work.

Harness optimization usually runs offline, so it needs a representative dataset and many expensive runs before the agent improves.

Exo moves that loop into normal task execution.

The agent edits its own harness code while it works. A small protected layer keeps the execution history and controls which policy version is active, so every change can be inspected.

title: Physical Superintelligence Solves Aaronson-Ambainis Quantum Computing Conjecture
summary:
The AI research firm Physical Superintelligence used an unreleased model from Anthropic to identify a proof for a long-standing problem in quantum complexity. The research system reached a complete proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture within three days of operation, and the firm subsequently verified the results using the Lean theorem prover.

The finding establishes that quantum computers cannot achieve exponential query speedups on almost all random yes/no inputs, defining the limits of when quantum machines can realistically outperform classical computers. The conjecture had remained an open problem in the field of quantum computing since 2008.

title: UPDATE: Axiom Releases Computer-Verified Proof of Weil Conjectures to Validate Stacks Library
summary:
The AI startup Axiom has published a formalization of the proofs for the Weil conjectures (I-IV) in the Lean programming language, including a machine-checkable version of the Riemann Hypothesis over finite fields. The company stated the release serves as a test of the reusability of its a digital mathematical library, intended to prove that AI agents can build complex new theorems on top of an existing verified foundation.

The conjectures were formalized using the Stacks Project library, an open-source encyclopedia of algebraic geometry that Axiom recently converted into 16M lines of machine-verifiable code. To maintain the project's interconnected structure, Axiom utilized a swarm of AI agents tasked with architecture, core definitions, and individual proofs under human supervision, creating a system where computers can confirm the logic of a mathematical result line by line.

Vibe coding at scale has a reputation for slop, so Axiom Math formalized the Stacks Project to show otherwise.

Mathematicians usually trust a proof because experts read it; Axiom Math turned an entire field’s reference book into Lean code, so a computer can now confirm the logic line by line.

Axiom ran its agent swarm like an engineering org, with humans assigning some agents the architecture, others core definitions and others individual proofs.

Lean checks every completed proof, and each tagged result links to its original text and dependencies, so the pieces fit together like panes of the Louvre’s pyramid.

And nothing entered the library unless the logic held.

All these means that now we have a free, open-source library where a big chunk of modern algebraic geometry exists as computer-checked code instead of only as text in a book.

In practice, anyone (a mathematician or an AI model) who wants to prove something new in this field can now reuse these already-verified definitions and theorems instead of rebuilding them, and a computer will flag any step that doesn’t follow.

title: Allen AI Launches ToyBlocks Robot Learning Simulator With 85K Training Demos
summary:
The newly available simulated tabletop provides a framework for robotics researchers to identify the causes of policy failures by experimentally controlling training data and targeted evaluations. Developed by the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2), the platform called ToyBlocks is released as an open resource comprising simulation assets, evaluation code, and 85K long-horizon demonstrations to help robot learning models transition from virtual environments to physical hardware.

To test the system, Ai2 used robot models based on Molmo 2 and ManiFlow that were trained exclusively within the virtual environment to perform tasks with lettered blocks. The robots successfully spelled a word in 15 of 30 attempts on a physical robot, compared to a success rate of 111 of 200 in the simulation. Ai2 stated the results show that simulation-trained models can transfer to physical robots, although further trials are needed to improve the reliability of the transfer.

title: Newly Elected US Governors Pledge Construction Pauses for 158.6 GW of Data Center Pipeline
summary:
Planned digital infrastructure expansion in the US faces a significant regulatory hurdle as newly elected officials in nine states move to restrict the buildout of new AI facilities. These jurisdictions have pledged to halt or pause construction on a pipeline that includes 158.6 GW of capacity, accounting for approximately 41% of all planned data center projects in the country, according to market intelligence firm Cleanview. Texas is the most heavily affected, with 88.4 GW of capacity at risk, followed by Ohio with 21.9 GW and Georgia with 20.2 GW.

The proposed moratoria occur as spending on software and information-processing equipment has become a primary engine of US growth, with contributions to the economy currently exceeding those seen during the Dot-Com boom. While some regions are tightening restrictions to curb investment, other states such as Tennessee and South Carolina have elected pro-industry leaders, and Florida's Governor-elect Byron Donalds has pledged support for the sector. Analysts warn that while pauses could reduce the risk of an AI spending bubble, a sudden contraction in infrastructure investment could remove a critical source of wealth gains and growth.

title: Midterm Election Pushback Won't Slow OpenAI's Data Center Expansion

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The AI startup is currently seeking capital in a fundraising round that would set its pre-money valuation at $1.25T, even as it faces growing community opposition to its physical infrastructure. Sarah Friar, CFO of OpenAI, told CNBC that the company's continued spending on data centers is not dependent on the recent midterm election outcomes, as the organization remains constrained by a lack of computing power despite its enterprise business doubling in the third quarter.

To mitigate local backlash, the company has rebranded its facilities as "Compute Campuses" and introduced a National Community Compact. The new policy mandates that the company cover the full cost of electricity and grid upgrades for its company-owned sites, provide site-level reporting on water and noise, and end the use of most nondisclosure agreements with public officials. The shift follows a series of local ballot measures in 10 states where voters favored restrictions on data center development in 40 of 41 cases.

CEO Sam Altman told employees that he recognizes the public's reluctance to live near such sites and suggested that the company could locate future installations in deserts. In response to OpenAI's pledges, Meta noted that it had already committed to covering its own energy and water costs several years ago.

title: Google DeepMind AI Discovers New Weaknesses in Legacy 1024-bit RSA Encryption

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The Google DeepMind Science team used AI agents to uncover flaws in the mathematical foundations of older digital signature protections, reducing the resources required to compromise legacy encryption. Working with cryptanalysis experts, the team identified two weaknesses in 1024-bit RSA schemes: one that makes signature forgery approximately 1,600 times more efficient and another that cuts the average cost of factoring keys in large batches by about 30 times.

The findings, which were reached in a matter of weeks, are intended to help security defenders improve encryption standards before future threats emerge. DeepMind stated that the discovery illustrates the risk of relying on the assumed hardness of older cryptographic schemes, though the results do not affect the security of modern systems such as RSA 2048.

title: US Indicts 3 Men for $129M AI Fraud That Targeted Hospitals and Fintechs
summary:
Federal prosecutors have issued an indictment against three foreign nationals for their alleged roles in a sprawling corporate impersonation network that utilized generative AI to steal from global businesses. The US Department of Justice named Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan, and Guy Sheetrit as the defendants, who are charged with wire fraud and money laundering for using fake voices and images to deceive employees into transferring $129 million to fraudulent accounts. The suspects have been arrested in the UK and Spain and are currently awaiting extradition to the United States.

The victims of the scheme included two US hospital systems and a UK fintech firm that lost $11.6 million. According to prosecutors, the defendants posed as CEOs and attorneys from international law firms, using a handwritten script titled "Lawyer Call" to discourage staff from alerting coworkers about the transactions. Once the money was transferred, the group routed the funds through international accounts and converted them into cryptocurrency to obscure the trail.

title: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small Tops Open Weight Models on ARC-AGI-2 With 81.7% Score
summary:
Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling 2 Small scored 81.7% on ARC-AGI-2 at $0.27 per task and 96.5% on ARC-AGI-1 at $0.08 per task in verified ARC Prize testing, outperforming every open weight model the organization has evaluated on both benchmarks. The 594B parameter mixture-of-experts model uses 17B active parameters and is available now for inference and fine-tuning on the company's Tinker platform ahead of an Apache 2.0 weight release scheduled for next week.

The ARC-AGI results add to earlier evaluations in which Inkling 2 Small scored 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, up 18 points from its predecessor to rank as the highest scoring open weight model developed outside China. It also placed first among open weight models on DesignArena with a 1,376 Elo rating and on Vals AI's Finance Agent and Finance Index, while averaging about 150,000 output tokens and $1.18 per Intelligence Index task at pricing of $0.30 per 1 million input tokens and $1.00 per 1 million output tokens.

Thinking Machines pretrained the model's main phase on 8.4 trillion tokens in 68 hours on GB300 chips in NVFP4 precision and included a launch blocking evaluation for customizability. Co-founder John Schulman said the team applied supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning alignment fixes before launch after early checkpoints "took unexpected actions to circumvent guardrails during training and evals."

Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Small, scoring 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index - their plan to release its weights would make it the highest-scoring open weights model developed outside China based on current rankings

Inkling 2 Small is launching as a proprietary model, available first-party through @thinkingmachines' Tinker platform and Tinker Playground, with weights to be released at a later date. Its score is up 18 points from Inkling Small, with ~4x as many output tokens per task. It matches @GoogleDeepMind's Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) and surpasses @XiaomiMiMo's MiMo-V2.6-Pro on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1.

Key takeaways:

➤ Large gains over Inkling Small, especially on agentic tasks: AutomationBench-AA rises from 5% to 46% and FrontierCode 2.0 from 5% to 25%. HLE-Diamond also rises from 12% to 29%.

➤ Different coding strengths from Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium): Inkling 2 Small scores 25% on FrontierCode 2.0 vs. 11% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium), but 13% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 vs. 30%.

➤ Creative agentic scores above Claude Haiku 5.5 and Grok 4.7 on AA-3D: Inkling 2 Small also scores above Gemini 3.8 Flash on both AA-3D and Code2Video-AA, but behind Claude Sonnet 5.5 on both.

➤ Research-level physics improves, but trails Gemini 3.8 Flash (high): Inkling 2 Small scores 56% on CritPt v2, up from 34% for Inkling Small, vs. 65% for Gemini 3.8 Flash (high).

➤ Fewer hallucinations from more selective answering: On AA-Omniscience v1.1, the hallucination rate falls from Inkling Small's 61% to 27%, while accuracy rises from 32% to 34% and the attempt rate falls from 77% to 53%.

➤ ~4x as many output tokens: Inkling 2 Small averages ~150K output tokens per Intelligence Index task vs. ~37K for Inkling Small, ~31K for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium), and ~99K for Gemini 3.8 Flash (high).

➤ Almost 6x the cost of Inkling Small, but cheaper than several other models with similar Intelligence Index scores: Inkling 2 Small costs $1.18 per Intelligence Index task vs. $0.20 for Inkling Small, $7.77 for Gemini 3.8 Flash (high), and $10.02 for Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium).

Key model details:

➤ Type: Proprietary reasoning model at launch; Apache 2.0 weights release planned

➤ Modalities: Text and image input, text output

➤ Size: 594B total parameters / 17B active parameters

➤ Pricing: $0.30/$1.00 per 1M input/output tokens ($0.03 per 1M cached input tokens)

➤ Availability at launch: Tinker and Tinker Playground

Congratulations to the team at @thinkingmachines on the release!

Proud to release our new model, Inkling 2 Small. Check out our blog post -- it includes a lot of detail about our training process.

To me, the most interesting part of this release was what we learned about alignment, which you can read about in the sections "Safety and alignment" and "Training Inkling 2 Small".

We experienced some unpleasant surprises when our early checkpoints took unexpected actions to circumvent guardrails during training and evals. We realized our capabilities-focused RL was training them to be extremely persistent and to succeed at tasks at all costs. Offline monitors first flagged this behavior, but later we realized it was happening frequently and was easy to replicate.

Before this release, we sprinted on a range of alignment interventions, from SFT to RL. These are briefly described in the blog post. We made a lot of progress, with big improvements on our own alignment evals and on previously unseen evals from external evaluators like Apollo and Goodhart.

We have a long way to go in developing alignment techniques that keep pace with the increases in model intelligence and training scale. We hope to share these techniques to improve the ecosystem. We also have a business reason: our goal with Tinker is to enable many people to do their own large-scale post-training, and we need to help them to do this without incident. Join us if you'd like to build this public science and practice of alignment. https://t.co/LdjsDFRZIN

title: SpaceX Plans 2027 Launch of Space-Based AI Computers Co-Designed With Nvidia

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
SpaceX is partnering with Nvidia to build AI computing centers that will operate in orbit to bypass power constraints on Earth. The aerospace company targets the third quarter of 2027 to begin deploying the hardware, with volumes slated to ramp up in 2028 and 2029, according to CEO Elon Musk. Musk noted that orbital sites provide 30% more solar power than ground-based facilities and that the cost of producing intelligence in space is lower once the cost per ton to orbit is reduced.

Investor Ron Baron expressed support for the move, arguing that the U.S. must increase domestic chip production and electricity generation to compete with China. Baron estimated that China adds approximately 300 gigawatts of power capacity annually compared with 20 gigawatts in the U.S., and that China's total power capacity is roughly three times that of the U.S.

title: Google Plans 2.7 GW Power Capacity for New $17B Wyoming AI Campus

summary:
Google is establishing its first Wyoming data center hub with a plan to build a computing campus on 716 acres in Laramie County. Known as Project Tembo, the $17 billion venture will consist of four data center halls near Cheyenne and is scheduled to begin operation in the second half of 2028. The facility is expected to start with a power capacity of 2.7 GW, though company plans include eventually scaling the site's capacity to 10 GW by the time construction is completed in 2031.

The project is expected to create roughly 3,700 annual jobs, though Google will hire only 250 employees directly. Statewide construction for the hub will support more than 8,800 jobs, with about 2,500 workers on site during peak building phases. To bring the project to fruition, Google acquired the land and regulatory approvals from developer Crusoe, assuming direct control of the site's management.

To power the campus, American Electric Power will invest $4B in a 702 MW natural gas fuel cell plant utilizing Bloom Energy cells under a 20 year agreement. To mitigate environmental impact, Google will use air-cooling systems to save water and route captured carbon to a sequestration hub operated by Tallgrass Energy. The company stated it will pay for all electricity consumed and infrastructure costs driven by the growth of the site.

title: OpenAI Debuts BioBasicsBench to Test AI Agents on Raw Laboratory Science Data
summary:
OpenAI has released a new evaluation framework called BioBasicsBench to measure the ability of AI agents to handle routine analyses in "wet-lab" biological research. Created with enzyme-design firm Ligo, the benchmark consists of 100 tasks based on real experiments that require models to interpret raw laboratory data, such as microscopy videos and gel photos, to spot errors or determine if the available evidence supports a conclusion.

In initial tests, OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra earned 66.7% of the available credit on the benchmark, outperforming the 43.8% scored by the GPT-5.6 Sol model. Astra used 4,704 output tokens per task at the xhigh setting—roughly half the output of Sol—though the newer model still failed certain tests by selecting the wrong DNA clones.

title: OpenAI's Restricted GPT-6 Sol Tops Vals AI Cyber Test as Open Weight DeepSeek Trails Close Behind at a Tenth the Cost
summary:
OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol, available only through its restricted Daybreak cybersecurity program, completed a leading 80.8% of objectives in Vals AI cyber evaluations, while the publicly downloadable DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 model reached 72.8% at under $3 per run compared with about $22 for Daybreak. On the Nova test, DeepSeek matched Daybreak's score, while on the Lighthouse exercise Daybreak breached a company, took administrator control, stole passwords and reached a second firm to complete 27 of 31 objectives in under three hours, versus 21 objectives for DeepSeek.

Vals AI noted that because open model weights are public, no provider can monitor or block their misuse, and that short evaluations understate open models because DeepSeek completed zero objectives in its first 25 million tokens before making most of its progress after 100 million tokens. Vals AI said it expects AI attacks on live networks to become more common in the coming months and urged defenders to use the models to test and patch their own systems first.

The benchmark results follow OpenAI's rollout of GPT-6 Cyber to vetted Daybreak Red customers, including security teams at Mozilla, Palo Alto Networks and Cisco, as well as offensive security partner Hacktron. Rated Critical on OpenAI's cybersecurity risk scale, GPT-6 Cyber identified 81 previously unknown high severity vulnerabilities in Firefox and generated working root exploits and candidate patches for 948 local privilege escalation flaws in the Linux kernel during a single $1.21 million API run.
